| | **UPDATE: Roughly 70,000 ballots left to count in CA-23 as margin shrinks. National Democrats rally behind Tessa.**
Hi, this is Tessa Lynn Hodge, Democrat who is on the verge of flipping CA-23, a congressional seat that Trump won by 19%.
In an extraordinary turn of events, we are inching closer to MAGA Rep. Jay Obernolte, and we have just been informed that there are roughly 70,000 more ballots left to count in our race.
National Democrats like Congressman Pete Aguilar, Chair of the House Democratic Caucus, are now fully behind our campaign. President Obama urged voters: "There is NO SUCH THING as a vote that doesn't matter... It takes time to count every ballot."
And that's exactly why Democrats are asking for your help. We need to make sure every ballot is counted. We need to hire monitors to watch the count, and a team to cure ballots that were rejected because they weren't signed correctly.
Can you please contribute what you can today so we can make sure they count every vote? It will go a long way in helping us close this 1% gap.

clean_body: Friend, We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy. The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded. At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong. We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation. I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down. I know you won't either! I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation. Landmark Legal Foundation is on a mission. They 're here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism . . . in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. And now, I'd love you to stand with me in supporting this outstanding organization. The Left aren't saviors of democracy.They 're Marxists. And what they're doing is destroying the country. They fight desperately to undermine our election processes and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for. They persecute their opponents, like when the Biden In justice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies. Leftists focus so much energy on the justice system - to control it, to contort it, to use it to promote their insanely radical agenda. Again and again, they turn to rogue left-wing judges to usurp the Constitution and undermine America's founding principles. We must not be silent while these leftists destroy our republic from within. That 's why it's so great to have Landmark Legal Foundation take them on! I love these guys. I've been part of the Landmark family for over three decades . . . as president for 20 years, then Chairman of the Board, and now Chairman Emeritus. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and help convince judges to do the right thing. In 2024, Landmark made a historic winning argument that special prosecutor Jack Smith lacked the legal authority to target Donald Trump in the classified documents probe. The judge in the case echoed Landmark's arguments in her decision and delivered a huge win over the Left 's lawfare. Landmark also fights to defend free, fair elections. For example, Landmark filed a supportive brief in another key election integrity case. With Bost v. Illinois Board of Elections , they're helping challenge unfair vote-by-mail procedures. Here, Illinois Congressman Mike Bost sued the Illinois Board of Elections over their practice of counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Such counting delays results and opens the door for abuse. When the Supreme Court agreed, it marked a major victory for free, fair elections. But this is not the last fight! This isn't political . . . it 's about the Constitution! My Landmark friends are on the frontlines of the battle to preserve our country. They're a vital part of the conservative, constitutionalist force fighting for our country today. Your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of " Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." Thank you in advance for actively joining the fight! God Bless, Mark Levin Chairman Emeritus Landmark Legal Foundation Landmark Legal Foundation is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. All donations are tax-deductible.

body:
It’s understating things by a lot to say the last 14 years have been an uphill battle. When Gabby founded this organization the NRA and the gun lobby were ascendant.
#

Friend, Emma Brown here.
I wanted to touch base and level with you about where we are as an organization after the elections this week, because the results have required us to take another look at our plans in the weeks, months, and years ahead.
Full disclosure: We didn’t expect this.
It’s understating things by a lot to say the last 14 years have been an uphill battle. When Gabby founded this organization the NRA and the gun lobby were ascendant. They had virtually unlimited resources and a bench of candidates in every state, and at every level of government.
The fact that GIFFORDS has passed more than 820 gun safety laws in the years since is, frankly, incredible. But, even in our most optimistic forecasts, we expected that we’d still need to be ready for the same kind of fights next year.
As I write to you now, there will be at least 54 Democrats in the United States Senate in 2027. 234 Democrats in the House — and counting. Democrats made historic gains in state houses, breaking up super majorities and flipping chambers. Next year, 29 states will have Democratic governors.
So, I’m going to ask you to do something here. I’m asking you to consider what we have already accomplished, even as we had to fight tooth and nail for every inch of ground. And then I’m asking you to imagine what is possible now. Today.
We'll continue to be in touch as plans come together for next year, but I was hoping to be one of the first to ask you to pledge your support as we make those plans. We're still going to need a lot of help, and that starts with you.
**[So, please: Will you make a donation to GIFFORDS so we can hit the ground running in 2027? There is still so much to do, and we can't do it without you.](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261107-1-B&t=1&akid=12008%2E3935704%2EVOB8C6)**

name: Gabby Giffords
subject: The first call I received
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
I remember thinking how many others had probably gotten the same call, both in Arizona and around the country.
#

I’ll never forget this.
When I was first elected to the Arizona House of Representatives, one of the first calls I received was from the NRA. They told me they couldn’t wait to work with me, how excited they were to build a partnership, and how much support I’d get from them.
I remember thinking about how many others had probably gotten the same call, both in Arizona and around the country.
I look back on that now, having spent the last 14 years building an organization that would stand up to the NRA, their candidates, and the grip they had on our politics.
I know how many candidates and elected leaders get calls from GIFFORDS now, because I am the one making those calls. I know the courage it takes to stand with us, to choose to take action to protect your constituents. And I know that none of it would happen without you.
This is an organization that runs almost entirely on grassroots support. People who care, people who are willing to do something for change. And I am incredibly grateful for you. Because of you, we have an unprecedented opportunity to pass gun safety legislation over the next two years — even in states we never thought possible.
It is going to require a ton of work, and a ton of resources. It is going to be difficult. But it is possible. That is why I am writing, and it is why I am humbly asking you:
**[Please, make a donation to GIFFORDS as we prepare for what may be the most active year in the history of our organization. $3, or anything you can afford. These gifts will add up fast if enough people chip in, and that’s what we need to make the most of this opportunity.](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261108-1-B&t=1&akid=12009%2E3935704%2ELY8y9q)**

name: Jane Fonda
subject: All eyes on Texas! 👀
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee
body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=21%2E6803%2EQTn07A)
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261108-ak.51A7aA&refcode=20261108-21&t=3&akid=21%2E6803%2EQTn07A)
We’re still celebrating Tuesday’s historic wins. I’m walking on air, light as a feather, breathing easier. I’m so proud of us, the American people, for proving so decisively we do not tolerate corruption, cruelty, and crimes.
Now there’s one race I need to talk to you about because it didn’t get sufficient attention in the “**BLEXAS** ” wave: **Congresswoman-elect Katy Padilla Stout (TX-23).**
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261108-ak.51A7aA&refcode=20261108-21&t=4&akid=21%2E6803%2EQTn07A)
Texas’ 23rd district stretches hundreds of miles along the US-Mexico border and encompasses one of our country’s most precious natural spaces: Big Bend National Park.
Trump and his polluter allies had their sights set on tearing right through it with bulldozers and border walls — threatening wildlife, fragile ecosystems, and the Rio Grande. And Katy’s opponent, right-wing gun influencer Brandon Herrera, was ready to rubber-stamp that destruction all while chasing YouTube clicks for his own benefit.
But this past Tuesday, the people of South and West Texas said heck no and rejected the low-effort agenda Brandon and Trump offered.
**Instead, they elected Katy – the first Latina to represent San Antonio and Texas’s 23rd Congressional District in the United States Congress. Wow.**
As a former kindergarten teacher and child welfare attorney, she ran unapologetically to protect her community, defend our public lands, and hold corporate interests accountable. **This district was once considered “deep red” – one that Donald Trump won by 15 points in 2024.**
But Texans made their voices heard loud and clear. And with Katy in Congress, I know she’ll faithfully carry her constituents' voices to Washington from the second she sets foot in Congress.
She’s already proving so:
[](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261108-ak.51A7aA&refcode=20261108-21&t=5&akid=21%2E6803%2EQTn07A)
That’s my kind of woman! Nothing gives me more hope than seeing our endorsed candidates waste no time holding the crooks accountable.
That’s exactly why I started JanePAC: to recruit, support, and elect leaders like Katy with the moral courage to fight like hell for our communities and our planet. We proved what people power can accomplish in TX-23 — and this is something we can achieve _everywhere._
Thank you for restoring hope.
In solidarity,
xx Jane
**Before you go...** I couldn’t be prouder of this grassroots movement. But Big Oil isn’t going to roll over and take their losses on the chin. Our newly elected leaders need us behind them on Day One to hold the line. **[So, as we celebrate these wins, can I count on you to throw in any amount to help us protect our victories and elect more leaders like Katy to Congress?](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261108-ak.51A7aA&refcode=em20261108-21&t=6&akid=21%2E6803%2EQTn07A)** **[Donate ››](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261108-ak.51A7aA&refcode=20261108-21&t=7&akid=21%2E6803%2EQTn07A)**

## Neighbors Help Flood Recovery Efforts
Water, shovels, and cash are headed to Copperhill after flash flooding [damaged 45 homes and 42 businesses in Polk County](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u7SAMB_CnSTaOgHwPDHc527lrx8gBE5AciIAmyttXOW2foIMX27L-P3-85hd48mH9DxuqUuwc8MyEpWCaLcVoEup4YLpMJLrOGI0lP0sueyYE4-MMuvgD5xZqoxYpJmh1jUoMUyuaXsi-dgpl20k9Sm6xAS4sh0b0XTMOXWM0dLL26j4oBB_vapvH0NlF8GWQ42S17UTVcjS-xPQoDguGgDkjWrruaA8dt5qUK2XPVfOvks9KPm-GdhAC0nQv_LS-ZcyAp6uSz18cW3D1ITOw9_Tt9mFlBg_IBQpmpuO-Y3KeiG1aw5UPT4TMYcLMXDzZFT-ZhsAc0l4nZfbTE_ncD1XL1w08vWOWP_74UPIrAAD__-hVlmg). Torrential rain sent the Ocoee River [to a record 18.05 feet Thursday](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpSAQRp8GO4wgKhYU29jdbbc0CINOgnIDs5L79htvsS_wF1PNl5OT8-e1vixGvPbf9gRDFNYLaolABHkNMSWfwaUb8senGD81JR8irrKTIxeCd3q1jvCGVdnGm02K2SrXgBHTrEQ_Cjk2hxnc0IPQelSz09qFHjY1T5Pbxnmb9eQbNA9QiE4_p_p2GsImum2Seg4uDIKpDjxSyi0dQHBdUApAiJ9HrXXpbKI5iN6F9b-YXJhcaq1tLef9PJlcHj6TixBMLt3A5LKnm0cAXsgS8BQCOrSx8AzlnS7PDyyUMjr-jYDXzinjvkP-TtxfKPy_B5NLk41_V4wRyzgx1e2nxfgVox9WvY38FwAA___q6Y4u), topping a mark set in 1990. Swift-water teams rescued more than 100 people and 25 dogs across Tennessee and Georgia. Mayor Greg Barker says money helps most right now, through the city’s disaster relief fund at People’s First Bank. In Chattanooga, a ModWash car wash [is collecting supplies through Nov. 14](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkM-OrSAMh58GdxhA_LdgcTfuzt3O0iAWJalioKM5bz_hJPMEs2jSJk37_b6v1_yyAcO5_bcHGCI_n_BkBCJIs8cY1wQu3pDea0R8PzGuHsOshOq4lFwMs3UUbpi1rVazKDla7Sowsh-1bDqpumo346K7Tlg99EPbjE44cAKWcWytUoNyUAVTDkophlK6qfvWL1IsvRpG73wrmRawBoqpph0IzhNyBvD4Lmi1i0eFZie6Mmv-MTUxNT3PU1M4IPsEcCXIuawxNZV8TE3lYZnizdQkSut2S2TPGDfLnU38sXnnLiKCo8zz93VhgMxt5i5eF6Q9IPIFtnBm_jHFf1UxNVXJrNcTEEPueqbFdtiAH1D6o-XbqJ8AAAD__4szlI4) for its district manager to deliver Nov. 15. Tellico Plains, which flooded in 2021 and 2023, [is gathering water, gloves, and shovels](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OnDAQRZ_GdEaewctP4SIN3aZNiYw9BksGr_AExNtHbJEX-Irbnnt0_rynt40p7stvu5FhDtNOV0nETMcUUs7-IJdPOm6fU7qvnH1IcUKFrQSQqp-s43jSpG3lzYwwWO0qMtANGpoWsK1Wo9sZh9n1gTz6oHsP3rumtQiNBQhdFc0DBFD9M93U3SvMoOYO-yG48AKhFfnI-ah5JaZ9p1KIQroftdrlrUpmZf4U0fwSOAocr-uqrzNxzafA8cELHAEEjqoTOGol17xRkfPfEr-0IuP2sY7Jy_mWtNGx0O5uGZItq_ymiPsi_58LHKvD-M8VU4ql7YRWy2Zj-trwD1OeBv8FAAD__xmjidw) for Copperhill. Mayor Marilyn Parker said help “is still going to be needed four, five, six, seven months from now.”
## Carter County Lands State Housing Study
Carter County will get a [state-backed housing market study](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO5CAURL8GZ7QA4wcBwSbOetMNLR4Xmx0MFtzulv9-5PmFCSorlU6df8_1aWKKeftrDtCIYc3waQkQoa4hleIruPKGevmS0vUpxYcUV8HESDmnbF6Nw_iGVZrOayu4MtJ1oPmkJO9HLsZu18IG5ZkclJV9AOG8HcFz6-ys3ATT3EV9D3LO5juyf0xDsJzZScwquDBwIhn4iKU-cAeEnKE1gJCuG-3hytElvSOejfR_iFiIWP6XPbeSXcTrrNDaXSJiud8RsciBqXEiYnGmIlTqyivjRTfARhsaBLpDOmkole7l1WLe6GHqFyBt-PIXEUtXtT8_MaXYxolIth0mph8S_KXGtxbfAQAA__-eU4qX) to pin down how many homes it needs to keep pace with growth. The Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development (TNECD) [picked 14 counties for the studies](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uwyAQx5_G3ojMh8EeGLpkS9eOFoYjRj1DBJdEfvvKlfoEHW65v_T7f3zdlptLmPL90-1gieKS4d0QiKAuEUsJFXx5QT1CQTzepYSIaRGD0IxzNkyL85ResCjXB7sKPjvle7DczIpLzYXuN2tWoWcT4uy1nKMcIRip_ODWSa56DK5P9gRyPkznKXkxY1z5sBoxzdHHkXdqgJCo1AttQJAztAYQ8TijXXzZe7Qb0aN18qMT105cKYMPp9KJ61np78VczuWZPTTGFfPlmSlBYw0QPEFgsVS2lWdL-c52V7-BmMsOjwYnoq82PN4JMTVtOjXcd5fw15_-Od7Lip8AAAD__8-ehs4), including Sullivan, Unicoi, Greene, and Cocke in East Tennessee. A consulting firm will visit each county and gauge demand for everything from rentals to single-family homes. Carter’s [application came from Noah Morrison](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO5CAURL8GZ7QA41dAsImz3nRDi8eljfYaWnC7W56vH3l-YYLKSlVH5999u9uEKT_-2gMMUdwyfBoCEdQtYimhgi9vqGcoiOenlBAxbUqokUvJxbxZT-kNm7ZdME7JxWrfgZHTomU_SjV2u5nEIsIUejv3o9Zy6V0Mw6CX0TkdBxG7ZK5BKcV8Rfe3aYhOCjepeYk-DpJpASFRqTfagSBnaA0g4nmh3Xw5OjQ70bOx_g9TK1MrYPqyDminkq8CU-v1wdQqJVOr0Eyt3laCyn15ZTp5AwRPEHgslTeyBHwvr5bygx-2_gfiNls8W2pMrV014flJiKmNE9PicdiEPyD0S4tvo74DAAD__9Ath7Q), a state rural fellow who started in the county in August and will lead the work locally. Mayor Patty Woodby called the selection “an important step toward better understanding the housing needs of our community.” The state already ran the same studies for every [West Tennessee county](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkb2u2zAMRp_G3hSIsvyTwUOXbLdrR4OSqFgobQUSE8NvX_hune_AgcQ5BInvz9fyhYnT_vyNG80icdnpqEwiVJbIOYdCPn-onCEzn0fOIXJajDaDAlB6WtBL-tBisQ2zM3BH61uaYbxb6AYwQ7vOLvRgEDRMqAfrpkjBBRvBOtdr6nSb5mshgJ6ust1t7KMD7UYz3aOPPTRWU0iSy01WEtp3qpUo8nmddvN5a3leRV616X415tGYx3EcF7vl9y6Y9lehWi-wMQ9OkaqcTPW_ZomE8i7f00ofKsjKX3qiqioxeaGgYi5qze-a9qfasPwlUbgjnzVdHhZJnmkxXjvvR6f60VnVj11QaKBX3k53O9g4Ag23VTZuyxxeR2JOdRgbq58bJv5-SH6Yxmc2_wIAAP__uB2jIA) to prepare for Ford’s BlueOval City truck plant. TNECD Assistant Commissioner Brooxie Carlton said that work showed “how valuable county-specific housing data can be” to local leaders planning for growth.
## Tennessee Layoff Notices Top 6,600 Workers
Tennessee employers have filed layoff or closure notices covering [6,655 workers so far this year](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGK9CAQwPGnMZ1BjatJYfE16fZrrwzGjBs5o4sOkbz9keO4F7hiYGDgx5_5eC5PG2JIr__2AIPolwStRkCEsviY81bA5RPKteUYr5bz5mNYBBOKck7ZuFiH4YRF2m4zq-CTla4Dw_Uk-aC4UN1uBjdNdljBj4orP0o9adCeaa3BrWJcu2BukHM23iOHXj_8ytmqxTh55x-cSAZbwFx63AEhJagVwMfrTutdPrpodsR3JcM_ImYi5tZa3-px3kci5tsnYuaciJnd2y9Cmy2JpozBQaXWe3BIj1yA4m4TVYox2nL5hFLpj9IVs71biDFUpYlkr8OG-F2Bf3zhacRXAAAA___EkYTb). Seven notices posted since mid-August account for 673 of those jobs, led by Wise Company in Hardin County with 129 and Kilgore Flares in Hardeman County with 127. Pepsi Bottling Group listed 112 Knox County workers, and Del Mar Medical filed the latest notice on Nov. 3, covering 52 in Wilson County. In Nashville, the [General Jackson Showboat will lay off 114 people](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLuunTAQRb_GdEYeY16FizR0N21K5Mf44MTgIzzB4e8jzi_cYqSRtrS09v71tX6ZmOLx-ml21ERhPbCWhER4riHl7E90-cLz9jmlu-bsQ4qrFHLgAFxMq3EUL1yVaby2EmajXIMaxllBN4Acmk2rYepg7o2xqhe2VxOMVvXBBA9CznZqon6AAGJ6TnXt2AcLwo5ymoMLPTAl0EfKZ0sbEh4HloIY0v2otS7vTdIb0buw7geTC5NLrbWtZb-ekMnl4TO5gHh-YHIpZAh5-HTnAIonc-cQCsd_b3SEnps9ev7CA0-T-G_j_pR88LLlarMh7lIuf09kcmlO7d81phTLMDIlXruJ6eNE3xz00vJ_AAAA__8Zt4rZ) when it docks for good Dec. 15 after more than 40 years on the Cumberland River. Paint maker Akzo Nobel listed 76 more Davidson County jobs ending Dec. 31. The notices warn of upcoming closings and mass layoffs, so not every listed worker is out of a job yet. Earlier filings covered 250 workers at TikTok's Nashville office and 325 at Carlex in Monroe County.

## Virginia Beach Tourism Tops $4 Billion
Tourism had a [$4 billion economic impact](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2PozAQhn-N6YzsYTBQuLiGLtdeiSZmCCMZHIEPlH-_IspWW245H3r0Pu-_23AjibI-_tLCPh_TsPK5R86Zt-HOFOac_m-yL_eUlp3WMKdtnwYw4LS12rQDhSwHD0jF6CdCpq5gb5sObeUqrIvZB1c12E0tggnoptrY0DYEo3WMODZciL941prWWgtQldCOzmFLbWfHusag0PAoOW1lnvmQ7SGr0BRf6eCtDGkpop9zfu6q-qOgV9Cf51medLyuo4L-clLQxxQo6s_wjdFvyx8L_fHWs2SN-i4xSlo1h7SmRYKW5Ukha1k1GKgV9MXmx-d5ve2uUWgeC0l8h8u_7PXw8BUAAP__JyyOZQ) in Virginia Beach in 2025, according to a report Visit Virginia Beach released Thursday. The city drew 14.4 million visitors, up 0.6% from 2024, and they spent an average of $7.2 million a day. Tourism supported 34,704 jobs, nearly one in five in the city, and generated $352.3 million in state and local taxes. That's up from a [$3.9 billion impact](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAQRU9jOpBtbDCFizR0mzYlGsywjGTwyp4F5fbRrpITpH_6X-993aYbUKTj_gk7ej7X6cCrRGTGPM0IYeP0zFT2OaW9wBG2lMs6aam7WqlaugkC04mTgWrxKxiEoUKv-sGotmuNrTYvcTHdMMPaSaNma63ue-d6GVywympZkX_tKSWdUkrrttFu6TrjwA1qsdYEYSQuxCk3vOFJ-U4HwRq_04m5CWmvot-YH0W0H0KPQo_XdTUnFeI_-K3yQoUeH5D5wFxnLOmZAxahx8LAWKe1_tUVeqyyXx4XxUil64WR9x0ovt_4n6FOr38CAAD__-6CfvM) in [2024](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOqzAQRb_GdEa2MQ4ULl5Dl9duiQYzwEjGjswEtH-_SrT5gu2Pju65X_fxDhQprf9hR8_nMia8jojMWMYJIWycn4WOfcp5PyCFLZdjGY0yTmotVTdCYDpxtFDNfgGL0Ffo9a23unGNbavNu2Db2XUwaQVm6s0UJlSL7kCB6-ewVORfPq1Vp7U2pqlNNztnO-h6PbetDcIqnIlzqXnDk8pKiWCJ3_nEUoe8V9FvzI9DNP-EGYQZPsy7oF7zKcwQckoYWJjhlSjM8FsmQ05M6YmH5CyXJ0aJIae8U5BryRdvkpL8GOVbKS_iTTaynyRnhihpf0DgF2iUsVXx8-OiGOlwN2HVugPF91D-48enNz8BAAD__wR7lN8), when 14.3 million people visited.
## Richmond Anchor Signs Off after 42 Years

**Whatever happened to _TV Guide_?** For roughly three decades, the best-selling magazine in America was a little digest that lived on top of the television set. At its 1977 peak, one in every five magazines sold in the country was a _TV Guide_. Walter Annenberg launched it nationally on April 3, 1953, for 15 cents, with Lucille Ball's [new baby on the cover](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykk8mWqjoUhp8mzk6tNIRm4CAoVFFVWtgcFSeuABGioRFCUz79XXIe4U7S7P3n-9Pt4-qy4lLJMlvzQsz1tbqUYmiV0Fo0l6ZK7uIqlBJNIkotmlTEnW51c8EQm38Q-gPtC0-07MUFzdL5VQgsyEzMkeUYiFjEorN8bjmmRS2KiQ1tkzuYWInlIHwl0DChYVszOX_hEII2Qtgh9A1xxyQoRYlIU0gpBwYUqdRV83arZKlzcVW_VS-at6QqZmqea123gDCAfYD9YRjeRMx_X0mAfalfrQEtQpBBIUYUEP_S3gdAlroH2M06mQrVJVIpAbAbc6WmLv4F2E2qXogGYFPqohCaA7KEaGWGEXJX-wMxGYWRv4jw2vMOFsBmztsckKXUoqAiNVObp6YFCMsAYREeGBO7oRzPNQ2L4B-1bmpAlqJMAKaEsQ37Zoy5bPGxzv5K6QFMsX_b5Gq55yvJUvEKuCxOTqtbsw-e03R0uklX-cNoi5o1mI3LIhWPY0uDp8ySRVKG42jaO7fr4E39cFrVbs8d_V6xifA87qTGB08FmfHjR-yRdWEgn9sIJ33QqsUqWESP6Dq5RJyvvn72h8-_6hzd9_ef3rdlBxkshb_76mxWFL-bdpLuvt_br0e49vvoXAe2_IDeie5pvpmyNo8n84f36de29urN6Ode7o7PT7kI7Di19ydq58flTb1vg49tGZqraYEIZU--nWk7bmZ0m0QeTm5cTTg_PFtVb0cQ9uv4e5Kg7_0Dj6cqzMbuo3wUTfqjwg9v8EJ417yrztf15yTcKLU9Hgwzfc-jfxe9nJCmqKiaRvHrYOQVtRb6Xk-P5t6d3dYxrTw1EWezZp7Wg1RKtqYFDJgVXKrpp-r_V1_9HP8XAAD__x37KKk). The trick was localization. National feature pages were printed once, then wrapped around more than 140 locally printed listings sections, so the copy on your coffee table was genuinely yours, right down to the UHF station nobody else got. It became a keepsake, not just a schedule. The January 25, 1964 issue carried [_" America's Long Vigil,"_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1u4zAQR_HTUJ0FDqnPgsU26rztlgJ3-KfFhBYNamLFtw-SK-QC7wG_f9f16lNO--2vv8NJLOuO88gQQV1r4XdE5IzK2AU14P-HHFJXo81wIbroafUs6YmVmuAiYGAbOBrnjuxox77ZHPcg6oFxJB6YuQvBgG00PkSaNDfJfeeI9ERkZtu35OfBUiBGCLrvveo0QpJS27eSdtkQ86s8UVsu9ya7TeRxKPtHmUWZ5TzPVjZs2OsrlhraUm_KLFxyBksq-6HMgs9HLhXKLL5Kip5FmcVO2s6mqS48zpRzOoZRdfp29yn_nOR3Pk9nvgIAAP__HyR7nQ) a 27-page record of the four days of Kennedy assassination coverage, introduced by President Johnson, and millions of families saved it. What killed publishing's golden goose? The "Guide" button on the cable box. Hundreds of cable channels made full listings impossible, and on-screen program guides made them unnecessary. Circulation fell from 20 million to 3 million through the 1980s and 1990s. Media mogul Rupert Murdoch had paid $3.2 billion for it in 1988. In October 2008, an SEC filing revealed the magazine's new price: exactly $1, plus roughly $100 million in assumed debt. Though its cultural cachet is gone, it never really died. _TV Guide Magazine_ still publishes from Troy, Michigan, about 24 issues a year, with circulation near 940,000, scheduling grids and all. For roughly three decades, the best-selling magazine in America was a little digest that lived on top of the television set. At its 1977 peak, one in every five magazines sold in the country was a TV Guide. Walter Annenberg launched it nationally on April 3, 1953, for 15 cents, with Lucille Ball's . The trick was localization. National feature pages were printed once, then wrapped around more than 140 locally printed listings sections, so the copy on your coffee table was genuinely yours, right down to the UHF station nobody else got. It became a keepsake, not just a schedule. The January 25, 1964 issue carried a 27-page record of the four days of Kennedy assassination coverage, introduced by President Johnson, and millions of families saved it. And every September, the eagerly awaited Fall Preview issue arrived, twice its normal thickness and often the biggest seller of any magazine in America. Usually the kids got to it first, circling the new shows they wanted to watch like a TV wish book. . What killed publishing's golden goose? The "Guide" button on the cable box. Hundreds of cable channels made full listings impossible, and on-screen program guides made them unnecessary. Circulation fell from 20 million to 3 million through the 1980s and 1990s. Media mogul Rupert Murdoch had paid $3.2 billion for it in 1988. In October 2008, an SEC filing revealed the magazine's new price: exactly $1, plus roughly $100 million in assumed debt. Though its cultural cachet is gone, it never really died. TV Guide Magazine still publishes from Troy, Michigan, about 24 issues a year, with circulation near 940,000, scheduling grids and all. belongs to a company called Fandom. In August 2026 the national debt passed $40 trillion.1 It was not
voted on. There was no ceremony. Most Americans found out from a
headline, if they found out at all.

Somebody has to absorb it

A debt that size does not simply sit there. It gets serviced,
refinanced, and eventually dealt with — and there are only three
ways to deal with it: raise taxes, cut spending, or reduce the real
value of what is owed by letting the currency weaken. The first two
require Congress to do something unpopular on the record. The third
requires nobody to do anything at all.

That is why the figure matters to a retirement account rather than
just to a budget committee. Every dollar in your IRA is a claim
denominated in the same currency the debt is denominated in.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e783889/UaHR0cHM6Ly9vZmZlcnMuYmlzaG9wZ29sZGdyb3VwLmNvbS9kZWJ0Lw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDg/LbmNsNnZ3UzNlcA/qP3V0bV90ZXJtPURlYnQ0MFQmbGVhZF9zb3VyY2U9ZGVidCZwdWJsaXNoZXI9anBtXQ/gavBpRg/sfo2297ccaf
If the obligation is managed down in real terms, that happens through
your savings, not around them.

The evidence is already behind us. It takes roughly $1.95 today to
buy what a dollar bought in 2000.2 Nothing was confiscated. The unit
was simply worth less each year, and savers holding it carried the
cost quietly.

Gold is the one asset in this conversation with no issuer. No
treasury can print it, no company can dilute it, no counterparty can
default on it. Central banks themselves have been buying more than a
thousand tons a year.3 They are not doing it for the yield.

You are allowed to hold physical gold inside an IRA. Most savers
have never been told that, because the firms holding their money do
not sell it. The free 2026 Gold IRA Guide walks through exactly how a
rollover from an IRA, 401(k) or TSP works, which metals the IRS
allows, how insured depository storage works, and the mistakes that
cost retirees the most. It is free and it takes about thirty seconds
to request.

body:
I’m still in my robe, running on no sleep, and I can’t wait to talk to you about what Tennessee just did and what comes next!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/1f791a8bac39/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7364009?e=dc5f639d62)

Hey friends,I’m still in my robe, running on no sleep, and I can’t wait to talk to you about what Tennessee just did and what comes next!
[**[CLICK HERE to LISTEN NOW**]](https://us.list-manage.com/9wfDgFN1Iaf?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
****
[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/19Dapsav38G?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

When the first early vote numbers dropped in Knox County and I saw the early vote totals for Michaela Barnett, I started crying, because I knew we were seeing something Tennessee hadn't seen before. This week it's just me, walking you through election night: the close calls, the flips, and what the folks who ran as unapologetic progressives showed us about how to win.
I also talk about the [State House pickups](https://us.list-manage.com/dY8WY2OdgYa?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), Knoxville candidates who moved their districts by double digits, why Tennessee doesn't get the national investment Texas and Georgia do, and what we have to demand from the new majorities in Washington: bold leadership, accountability and real help with affordability. Plus the story of the sweetest, most polite postcard that sent Tim Burchett into a tailspin.
We did not win everything. But when we vote, we win, and I'm not done thanking every one of you who knocked a door, made a call and showed up.

Thank you for being here,
Gloria

## Sam Fox Trades Restaurants for Hotels
Phoenix restaurateur Sam Fox [has stepped away from Fox Restaurant Concepts](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkLuunTAQAL8GOh_hB3AoXKShu2lTIoPXYMl4kXfhwP366OYX0o9Go_nzNX25mGJef7sdLLvvMGX4UAJmKJPHjIXIXUDPfmyYH4-ZA5ZJNaoTUormPbmF4wWTcbW3uluG3tRgZT8YabTUpt7sDErJFnrtF2m63gywNP3cShfc8vZyrqP98UnZvKVuWq1e0g9etdrPvZQDDF1lGvCRsbx4A1fiN2YX0oMXlNeCe53sxnxQpX9VaqzUGPN8UsxAdGz3D1GpkYu7IIkEkc4ClRrJ7SLgLWiLgUkEXE4SjCKd91kesSFDEh4uSHjskFkETAk_Ma-iALE7i8ss1oLnIeCOXBfrj09MKVLXV6ZZdxfTvzz-37OXVX8DAAD__7a4lGM), the company he launched with one Tucson restaurant in 1998. Fox stayed on after selling the group to The Cheesecake Factory for [more than $350 million in 2019](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkLvOpDAUg58GuiBy4Vak2Ibu33ZLdEgOQ6SQoOQAwzz9inmFv_skW5btfz_TDzjvwusvbKgJPssU8MoeiTBNNoaYcoYT873tawy3jYGWmCZRi5Zxzup-AkPuxElBabVszdCpEjXvBsWV5FKVqx4sNJ00g-j4LFXf4MIl70W_tEIIMF3p9JPHed1zWTdSVNwOVjTSzh3nAw5toWq0jmKqaEVI7hMDLP6OJ6bKxK30eiXacyH_FGIsxHhdVwWz4c2jFmJ8NhVinI_sAuYHM2xsiW-Gb0f5SwkzwZEgEDMxGNwps8t5z5ZojsxiYGsk9Mwc3gVINzsx0JEwl0nb_XG63HaFql8bOP-tRb999NTifwAAAP___neO6w), and the pandemic kept him longer than planned. Over his run, the company created 22 brands, including Culinary Dropout and Flower Child, and opened 170 restaurants. His last day was Oct. 30, and [he’ll now focus on Author & Edit Hospitality](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuhDAURL8GOlZ-LdiFizR0mzYlutiXxYqxkX2XfXx9lFX-IN1IM5ojna_LdIEQQ7p-woaW4LVMCe81IhGWyeeUS61wYH1u-5rT0-dESy6TYKLvOO-YnsBROHBS0Hore2cG1aLlg1FcSS5Vu9p-cFob49msz0YJxYycZwDNvXbCD7oN9vePc6a5ZGcpTtwbL87SzwPnBk3fKIY-UC4nWhFKeOUES3zmA8vJ5a2NdiXaayM_GjE2YvwmeBeNGP_W3XyrIWGtjRgrbN2SHx0-AtV3KlgJbgUSdS4nhzvVtli_30OMofZDo9h1gxDfMPqvp8OKnwAAAP__PlJ_wg), which runs the 141-room Global Ambassador hotel in Phoenix. _“It's time for me to focus on things that I own 100% of,”_ Fox said. The Global Ambassador was Fox’s first hotel, which [has won a Michelin Key every year since opening in December 2023](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2unDAURldjOiP8M3goXKShe2lTohv7GqwYG9l3IMzqozdbSP19Ojo6v76WL4gp5vUn7GgJ3mHJeLWERFgXX3KprcGJ7d6PreTbl0yh1EUOcuRC8OG5gKN44qKh81aNbjK6QyvMpIVWQulus24wyptxfEzSK6-N1pN56uA8KO8EQBftN0-I4SnU8FCyF37y8qH8byPEhNPI9IA-Uqk9bQg1vkuGkO5yYu1d2btkN6KjMfWDyZnJ-bquPrS6wwrvmPH7w-QcEOhVkckZAmHlofzlFRvBq0Im7kp2eFDjDfbPFhuHF22lxrxy4Bkv_idmz0vgW2lHJEiRbibnrlp_XDGl2EbD9LDuENNHjP636WnlvwAAAP__GVGQNQ). Fox has hinted at a smaller sister hotel in Phoenix. He and Justin Timberlake plan to open a second Twelve Thirty Club, their Nashville supper club, in Austin, Texas, in 2027.
## Donors Bring Phoenix Symphony Back
The Phoenix Symphony will return to the stage Nov. 12 after local donors [pledged enough money to lift the suspension](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUBeCnwRsRf8ZhYOjiLV07outwHaNisIA6TZ6-itU-Qed7dY6-83FxFwgxpNs7rGgbPGeX8F4jtobF-ZxyqRV2rI91W3J6-JzanIsTTGjKOWVnB9cWdnQKOm-lvppBdWj5YBRXkkvVLVZMg0ZgSg0z46B742cDvdQKJ9FPE3bBvvI4Z2cuWS_FiXvjRS_9NHBu0GiiGPrQcjm1BaGEZ04wx0fesZyuee2iXVrbKpFvRIxEjJ8NjgMR4-83fbGIGLclYwrf9A9EC9avFSutCDUnepDpFtHfsHbF-u0eYgxVD0Sx2wohHoXtv1vtVvwEAAD__9vYgfA) of its 2026-27 season. The orchestra stopped playing after Nov. 1 and [laid off its 66 musicians without pay](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O5CAUBODT4AwLHrR_AoJNnPWmG1qvzbPNLgYLaHvbpx_1SDMXmLxU-qr-3Mc7Ou_C8hs3MgWveQx0Zk-lUBptDDHljAfl17avMbxsDGWOaQQBDZeSi27EqbiDRo2VNaqZ-lZXZGTba6mVVLpaDaG4AUoFbdshkiDd9TOBbRWK_iHmypl3n5Sik0rcFNTS9hZuyj5aKXvqG6YFWVdiqstKmNwVA87-FQ9K9RS3ypu1lD0z9YvBwGA4z7P-9_e66pgWBsPjmV2gnBkM3_CGwbCvkYL7z7_W8dN5zxPl50Z8pzTHtGGYKPNcMBUXFh7iwSVUydj9HXa5aZkWy4bOf0rKT088DHwEAAD__7G-iOo) the next day. Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.

_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.
---
[](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckc2OnTAMhZ8m7LjKP7BgUQnR1bSjbrqMTOJAVEhoEu68fsXMfYJu7eNj-zu_38wbhD3E9QccOK7pPE0u5gNdinWDJ2JM17olXzcsmIPhlOuWsZb2BmwNTzQSGjdK0FJr3eDIukEyKSnTzTZ67qzvUPTWOr9wxntQQLFXXjKlhW7CeBsyRnsmOGXywaXq6aIcLHahg1dEUnShpvy4b8tYgsNYA-wPm45mH7daz0LEN8JnwueC9sr4gIgu1VtB-FyvHENc2zOFWNurAOFzNyi_qA7bAQfRSnTQDoiiBd97r5ChRiBiLunKFo1NDomYvv98f__FVEdlR7i-6mEOdOE6iJjwgLC_il9DREwbZAfljwH799WycJwQ1kjEVM-rwBfCUI5PrC9RxXxbNnl050fY91B0RyRd7xWfT9f_jek58n8BAAD___2ho_k)
---
That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
---
[](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckc2OnTAMhZ8m7LjKP7BgUQnR1bSjbrqMTOJAVEhoEu68fsXMfYJu7eNj-zu_38wbhD3E9QccOK7pPE0u5gNdinWDJ2JM17olXzcsmIPhlOuWsZb2BmwNTzQSGjdK0FJr3eDIukEyKSnTzTZ67qzvUPTWOr9wxntQQLFXXjKlhW7CeBsyRnsmOGXywaXq6aIcLHahg1dEUnShpvy4b8tYgsNYA-wPm45mH7daz0LEN8JnwueC9sr4gIgu1VtB-FyvHENc2zOFWNurAOFzNyi_qA7bAQfRSnTQDoiiBd97r5ChRiBiLunKFo1NDomYvv98f__FVEdlR7i-6mEOdOE6iJjwgLC_il9DREwbZAfljwH799WycJwQ1kjEVM-rwBfCUI5PrC9RxXxbNnl050fY91B0RyRd7xWfT9f_jek58n8BAAD___2ho_k)
---
That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.

There are still outstanding races across the country, and we have several high-stakes races where recounts, ballot challenges, and legal fights will determine outcomes. The DLCC is working directly with our in-state programs and partners to ensure that we win these final races. 🎊 The Big Picture Victory:DLCC Flips 500+ State Legislative Seats In a stunning shift in power, the DLCC and state legislative Democrats flipped at least 500 seats in Tuesday’s elections. Alongside the seat flips, Democrats picked up majorities in at least 12 chambers and broke at least 13 GOP supermajorities. 🗳️ Minnesota Recount Alert:Democrats prepare for a recount after a 4-vote difference With only four votes separating Democrat Rob Kupec and his opponent, the DLCC is working to support recounts in the MN Senate that we expect to occur before the end of November. body:
Hey Peter, it's Scott.
I was born and raised in Mississippi. Growing up here, I never thought I would be locked in what is shaping up to be the closest Senate race in modern history.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261108-partner-sc.LTEM8M&amount=5&refcode=em20261108-1324&t=1&akid=1324%2E34582%2E7Ar4ZZ)
Getting here wasn’t easy.
But over the last fourteen months my campaign has traveled all across the state, speaking with every last voter we could find.
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261108-partner-sc.LTEM8M&amount=5&refcode=em20261108-1324&t=2&akid=1324%2E34582%2E7Ar4ZZ)

[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261108-partner-sc.LTEM8M&amount=5&refcode=em20261108-1324&t=3&akid=1324%2E34582%2E7Ar4ZZ)
Along the way we’ve been funded by grassroots donations of $5, $10, even $50 at a time. And it means the world to me to know that so many people have my back.
But this race isn’t over yet.
We need to make sure that we stand up for the will of the voters from now until this is fully certified. In a state like Mississippi, we can’t afford to get complacent at the finish line.
Closing this race out is going to cost millions of dollars. This is going to be the most closely divided U.S. Senate race in modern American history.

Friend, The 2026 midterms were a breakthrough for Democrats in the Senate. We flipped **SEVEN** Republican-held seats in Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina and Texas, including several states Trump won by double digits in 2024. According to an analysis by _The Cook Political Report_ , **"Voters in red, purple and blue states alike sent a clear message to Trump and the GOP-held Congress that they dislike the way they were governing the country and are willing to give Democrats the chance to steer things in a different direction."** This is a major step in the right direction. With a blue Senate majority, Democrats gain powerful tools to hold the administration accountable, protect our freedoms and deliver for working families. They can block or reshape legislation, refuse to advance administration nominees and scrutinize executive branch actions through hearings and investigations. **We’ve flipped Minnesota’s First Congressional District from red to blue.** I’m still taking it in.

This victory belongs to you, Peter. It belongs to the neighbors who knocked doors, chipped in what they could, hosted a living room conversation, put up a yard sign, or told a friend why this race mattered. Here’s why. Last week, days before the midterm elections, I wrote that the best thing Washington could do for markets was nothing. A divided government, with Congress controlled by Democrats, and the legislative paralysis that comes with it, would not necessarily be bad. For an overheated economy running on $6 diesel, 5% long bonds, and a stock market valued at well over twice GDP, the healthiest outcome might actually be gridlock.
On Tuesday, voters delivered exactly that. Democrats swept both chambers, flipping at least seven Senate seats, including Texas, where James Talarico beat Ken Paxton by 11 points. Kansas elected its first Democratic senator since 1932. It was the first time since Obama's second term that an incumbent president lost both chambers.
* * *
## [Good Gridlock](https://substack.com/redirect/35e01412-0936-4bdd-9304-b3975411a2f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| Nov 1
[](https://substack.com/redirect/35e01412-0936-4bdd-9304-b3975411a2f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[In the movie Wall Street, Gordon Gekko famously declares that "greed is good." But there is another g-word that the actual Wall Street might also love, and it isn't greed. It's gridlock. Not the kind on the Long Island Expressway or on Route 93 entering Boston at rush hour. The kind in Washington where one party holds the White House and the other holds...](https://substack.com/redirect/35e01412-0936-4bdd-9304-b3975411a2f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/35e01412-0936-4bdd-9304-b3975411a2f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
The Dow's first verdict was unambiguous: up 1,569 points on Wednesday, its best day since April 2025. Morgan Stanley put it simply: "Markets like gridlock." The market's fear index (the VIX) plunged 20%.
It lasted one day. On Thursday, the Dow plunged 1,833 points. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% into correction territory, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 12% in a session to lock in its fifth straight weekly decline. Wall Street's worst week since June arrived was the week it got the election result it had been rooting for.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/aabdb8b3-121a-4011-aa53-09e106d8f176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Both days were telling the truth, about two different markets. **The market got what it wanted on Tuesday. Then it remembered what it owns.** Wednesday priced restraint in Washington, and most of the economy liked it. Thursday priced restraint in Abilene, Texas, and every other county where a data center was being built. Turns out the one sector that has been carrying the index did not like gridlock.
**The First Market**
Start with the market that rallied. The winners on Wednesday were the sectors Republicans had been targeting, or taxing, or simply ignoring:
* _**Solar**_**.** Tax credits that Republicans planned to kill by 2028 are now safe.
* _**Hospitals and insurers**_**.** Hopes that Democrats restore the expired ACA subsidies.
* _**Dollar stores**_**.** A belief that tariffs stop escalating and stop taxing working-class consumers.
* _**Bonds**_**.** A bet that a divided Washington cannot spend at prior rates. The 10-year fell to a four-week low.

This is the broad economy, the ninety percent that doesn't build chips or server farms. It has spent two years absorbing tariffs, record diesel, and a Fed that couldn't cut. For that market, a Washington that does nothing is a gift. No new trade wars, no new deficit-financed subsidies, no fresh shocks to price. A narrower range of policy outcomes is exactly what a consumer-facing business, a hospital, or a bond investor wants.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/223d0fa3-3e96-4346-96f3-0b6e4a58bb77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**The Second Market**
Now the market that fell. For two years a handful of chipmakers, hyperscalers and data center builders have carried the S&P 500. Strip them out and the index has gone roughly nowhere. Their earnings, their capital spending, and their multiples are what turned a stagflationary economy into a record stock market. This narrow strength concealed the economic weakness that led voters to evict politicians they blamed for the affordability crisis.
In reality, the AI trade was never a bet on Washington staying out of the way. It was a bet on Washington staying in the way, on the right side: federal subsidies, fast-tracked permits, pre-empted local zoning, and a White House that treated every gigawatt as a national security asset. Unified Republican government was the AI trade's policy tailwind. Thursday's market showed us what it looks like when a tailwind turns into a headwind.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/0219419a-c484-4e46-b175-c3bc79cc1d95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In addition to chip and AI companies, other losers were the firms whose business model was proximity to power. Trump Media fell 25%. Tesla and SpaceX slipped on Wednesday, then fell 11% and 9% on Thursday. Musk poured over $150 million into the Texas Senate race and lost, and Texas going blue changes the landscape for the massive data center complex in Abilene. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on "an immediate moratorium on new data center construction." A Democratic Congress won't pass a national moratorium; Trump would veto it. It doesn't need to. The subsidies may stop and a slower and more expensive buildout is a valuation-adjusting change for a sector priced for faster and cheaper.
**So the sector most exposed to divided government is the sector the index can least afford to lose. Gridlock is good for most of the economy. The problem is that most of the economy isn 't what has been holding up the market.**
None of this is the French Revolution; nobody is lopping off heads. Trump still has the power to veto. Democrats lack a filibuster-proof majority. And that's precisely the point: the market isn't pricing in any sweeping legislation. It's pricing in **restraint** : no new tariff escalations, no more blank-check AI subsidies, and no more one-party fiscal policy that drives inflation and yields.
* * *
## [France on Fire (Again)](https://substack.com/redirect/c23ca810-fb77-495b-b23c-89df0a8b9a24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *
---|---|---
| Oct 25
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c23ca810-fb77-495b-b23c-89df0a8b9a24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[In 1972, a journalist asked Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai about the impact of the French Revolution. His answer, the story goes, was, "It's too early to say." The line has become a staple of geopolitical commentary. It's a great reminder that revolutions unfold on very long timelines (and that the Chinese generally think about dynamics over the long-term c...](https://substack.com/redirect/c23ca810-fb77-495b-b23c-89df0a8b9a24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/c23ca810-fb77-495b-b23c-89df0a8b9a24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
The economy isn't fixed. Diesel is still near records, the Buffett Indicator remains very elevated, the Strait of Hormuz continues to be effectively closed, and the Fed is likelier to hike than cut. But Washington just took its foot off the accelerator, and the VIX, which spiked to 26 on Thursday, is again drifting lower.
That is what reduced uncertainty looks like. Not calm, but rather a narrower distribution of outcomes. The tail scenario where Washington starts a new trade war, a new real war, or a new trillion-dollar subsidy before 2029 has been largely cut off. But the tail where a bubble built on cheap money and policy favor deflates on its own schedule has not. One of those tails was always Washington's to control. The other never was.

Gridlock is good for most of the economy. It is not good for the one sector holding up the index. | | | Nov 8 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Last week, days before the midterm elections, I wrote that the best thing Washington could do for markets was nothing. A divided government, with Congress controlled by Democrats, and the legislative paralysis that comes with it, would not necessarily be bad. For an overheated economy running on $6 diesel, 5% long bonds, and a stock market valued at well over twice GDP, the healthiest outcome might actually be gridlock. On Tuesday, voters delivered exactly that. Democrats swept both chambers, flipping at least seven Senate seats, including Texas, where James Talarico beat Ken Paxton by 11 points. Kansas elected its first Democratic senator since 1932. It was the first time since Obama's second term that an incumbent president lost both chambers. | | | | ---|---|--- | Nov 1 | The Dow's first verdict was unambiguous: up 1,569 points on Wednesday, its best day since April 2025. Morgan Stanley put it simply: "Markets like gridlock." The market's fear index (the VIX) plunged 20%. It lasted one day. On Thursday, the Dow plunged 1,833 points. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% into correction territory, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 12% in a session to lock in its fifth straight weekly decline. Wall Street's worst week since June arrived was the week it got the election result it had been rooting for. Both days were telling the truth, about two different markets. The market got what it wanted on Tuesday. Then it remembered what it owns. Wednesday priced restraint in Washington, and most of the economy liked it. Thursday priced restraint in Abilene, Texas, and every other county where a data center was being built. Turns out the one sector that has been carrying the index did not like gridlock. The First Market Start with the market that rallied. The winners on Wednesday were the sectors Republicans had been targeting, or taxing, or simply ignoring: Solar. Tax credits that Republicans planned to kill by 2028 are now safe. Hospitals and insurers. Hopes that Democrats restore the expired ACA subsidies. Dollar stores. A belief that tariffs stop escalating and stop taxing working-class consumers. Bonds. A bet that a divided Washington cannot spend at prior rates. The 10-year fell to a four-week low. This is the broad economy, the ninety percent that doesn't build chips or server farms. It has spent two years absorbing tariffs, record diesel, and a Fed that couldn't cut. For that market, a Washington that does nothing is a gift. No new trade wars, no new deficit-financed subsidies, no fresh shocks to price. A narrower range of policy outcomes is exactly what a consumer-facing business, a hospital, or a bond investor wants. The Second Market Now the market that fell. For two years a handful of chipmakers, hyperscalers and data center builders have carried the S&P 500. Strip them out and the index has gone roughly nowhere. Their earnings, their capital spending, and their multiples are what turned a stagflationary economy into a record stock market. This narrow strength concealed the economic weakness that led voters to evict politicians they blamed for the affordability crisis. In reality, the AI trade was never a bet on Washington staying out of the way. It was a bet on Washington staying in the way, on the right side: federal subsidies, fast-tracked permits, pre-empted local zoning, and a White House that treated every gigawatt as a national security asset. Unified Republican government was the AI trade's policy tailwind. Thursday's market showed us what it looks like when a tailwind turns into a headwind. In addition to chip and AI companies, other losers were the firms whose business model was proximity to power. Trump Media fell 25%. Tesla and SpaceX slipped on Wednesday, then fell 11% and 9% on Thursday. Musk poured over $150 million into the Texas Senate race and lost, and Texas going blue changes the landscape for the massive data center complex in Abilene. Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on "an immediate moratorium on new data center construction." A Democratic Congress won't pass a national moratorium; Trump would veto it. It doesn't need to. The subsidies may stop and a slower and more expensive buildout is a valuation-adjusting change for a sector priced for faster and cheaper. So the sector most exposed to divided government is the sector the index can least afford to lose. Gridlock is good for most of the economy. The problem is that most of the economy isn 't what has been holding up the market. None of this is the French Revolution; nobody is lopping off heads. Trump still has the power to veto. Democrats lack a filibuster-proof majority. And that's precisely the point: the market isn't pricing in any sweeping legislation. It's pricing in restraint : no new tariff escalations, no more blank-check AI subsidies, and no more one-party fiscal policy that drives inflation and yields. | | | | ---|---|--- | Oct 25 | The economy isn't fixed. Diesel is still near records, the Buffett Indicator remains very elevated, the Strait of Hormuz continues to be effectively closed, and the Fed is likelier to hike than cut. But Washington just took its foot off the accelerator, and the VIX, which spiked to 26 on Thursday, is again drifting lower. That is what reduced uncertainty looks like. Not calm, but rather a narrower distribution of outcomes. The tail scenario where Washington starts a new trade war, a new real war, or a new trillion-dollar subsidy before 2029 has been largely cut off. But the tail where a bubble built on cheap money and policy favor deflates on its own schedule has not. One of those tails was always Washington's to control. The other never was. | | ---|---|--- VIKRAM MANSHARAMANI is an entrepreneur, consultant, scholar, neighbor, husband, father, volunteer, and professional generalist who thinks in multiple-dimensions and looks beyond the short-term. Self-taught to think around corners and connect original dots, he spends his time speaking with global leaders in business, government, academia, and journalism. He 's currently the Chairman and CEO of Goodwell Foods, a manufacturer of private label frozen pizza. LinkedIn has twice listed him as its #1 Top Voice in Money & Finance, and Worth profiled him as one of the 100 Most Powerful People in Global Finance. Vikram earned a PhD From MIT, has taught at Yale and Harvard, and is the author of three books, , and . Vikram lives in Lincoln, New Hampshire with his wife and two children, where they can usually be found hiking or skiing. You're currently a free subscriber to . body:
| | | It's Chuck Schumer.

Against all odds, Democrats have won the majority.

This is a generational remake of the Senate map. So far, we've managed to flip **_seven seats_** ‐‐ Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, and Texas ‐‐ all while defending Michigan, New Hampshire, Georgia, and _every other Democratic ‐held seat._

**And we're not done yet:** Right now, the races in Alaska and Mississippi are still too close to call, and we could expand our new majority.

I have five words for the American people as we head into this new era: **Relief is on the way.**

You showed up to the polls to put a check on Donald Trump, his allies, and their agenda ‐‐ so my fellow Democrats and I are going to do our part. We are going to stand up to Trump's chaos, crack down on corruption, and work hard to drive down costs ‐‐ _the president can work with us if he chooses, or face another drubbing for his party in 2028._

This historic victory wouldn't have been possible without the support of dedicated Democrats like you. So from the bottom of my heart, thank you for showing up when it mattered, and for putting in the work to make our country a better place.

**Now, we need to keep this momentum going as we head into 2028. Republicans won't stop fighting, so we have to do everything in our power to defend the majority we worked so hard for.**

But I’ll be honest: That is going to take time – and plenty of resources that we don’t currently have. As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain the top target of the DC establishment. We put everything we had into winning this race, so I’m counting on your help to fight back against their attacks. It looks like we’re in this for the long haul, so I need your help to sustain our fight until every vote is counted. From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by grassroots donations from people like you. I’m proud of that fact, but it means it’s going to take lots of us to stand up to their pressure in the coming days. That’s why I have to ask: **[If you can afford it today, please pitch in anything you can to my and Elaine Luria’s campaign at this critical moment. Join us for a community call full of rest, reflection, and love notes | | | Peter, November is National Family Caregivers Month, a time to honor those who care for family members living with chronic illness, disability, or age-related needs. It’s also a reminder that caregiving can take a real toll on our mental health, and that the people who care for others deserve support, rest, and care of their own. And we know our community is full of caregivers. 💌 We’re the ones taking care of our parents and abuelitos, raising our siblings, and showing up for our loved ones. And this year, as this administration has torn through our neighborhoods, so many of us stepped up to hold our families together after a loved one was detained or deported. That’s why we’re coming together for****[**Powered by Community: A Space for Mental Health, Healing and Storytelling**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpnuOuFd62__J0jYpBRofRWUVV9ALH2OLsg-nS5A1PLxq7Nwo67VPTajx2psP0etL1XicePyLEMWle2uGytTU_qXHK-W28jtpgvKsBpO7PiScpMSEn0yt4XMvdmmY5RuXH-ki2ExuChttFOM4suFI0hLABnq9XHPjoOE7HeHnBFd0LXlWtIY3984vmteOmooKhelyfc0TFOfPgV90oYIQJiyZUTUCD78tOrXSR6irC_sMBHsWykEIe6_t5CdTbopFu/4vk/A2VIwKGAQiy7iKT_lyw7ew/h0/h001.f05TcR2xDthREpo1i_jMjPEXBonzD6BiGbs-YIQyP5Q) on Tuesday, November 10 at 7PM ET.
